name: Training the Beast
summary: In Mulgore, young tauren hunters learn to live and hunt beside a beast. After proving their patience and resolve by soothing the plains’ wild creatures, they travel to Thunder Bluff to learn the lasting bond of care and command.

sections.title: The Path to the Great Bluff
sections.body: After facing plainstriders, prairie stalkers, and swoops in Mulgore, tauren hunters are ready to take up the full mantle of the hunter. Yaw Sharpmane, their mentor in Bloodhoof Village, sends each novice to Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. There, Holt Thunderhorn teaches them. The shu'halo honor him for communing with the wilds, and his reverence for the Earthmother is greater still.

sections.title: A Sacred Bond
sections.body: To the tauren, a beast is a partner joined through harmony with the natural world, never a weapon or thrall. Holt Thunderhorn teaches hunters how to sustain that bond. They learn to guide a creature's combat instincts, feed it regularly, mend its injuries, and call its spirit back if it falls defending its companion on the plains.

faq.q: Who do I speak to for this quest?
faq.answer: Speak with Holt Thunderhorn atop Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. After your first trials taming wild beasts in Mulgore, Yaw Sharpmane sends you to him.

faq.q: What skills do tauren hunters learn upon completing this quest?
faq.answer: Holt Thunderhorn teaches you to train your companion in new abilities, feed it to keep it loyal and content, and revive it if it perishes in combat.

faq.q: Where does this quest fit in the tauren hunter chain?
faq.answer: This is the final step in the sequence. It follows The Hunter's Path and the three trials of Taming the Beast, where you temporarily pacify an adult plainstrider, a prairie stalker, and a swoop across the plains.

faq.q: Why does Holt Thunderhorn hold such high standing among tauren hunters?
faq.answer: Holt has spent a lifetime testing himself against Azeroth's fiercest beasts and commands several powerful companions. He also keeps a deep spiritual bond with the Earthmother, and his wisdom makes him the chief teacher of young shu'halo hunters in Thunder Bluff.

faq.q: Can hunters tame their permanent pet before turning in this quest?
aliases: can i tame a pet now
when do i get my pet
do i need training the beast
faq.answer: You can already tame wild beasts from the earlier trial, but until you speak with Holt Thunderhorn, you lack the knowledge to feed your companion, revive it, or teach it skills.

faq.q: Why is pet care tied to the Earthmother in tauren culture?
faq.answer: Tauren see every living creature as a child of the Earthmother. A hunter does not dominate a beast by sheer force of will, but enters a spiritual covenant, offering food and care in return for loyalty and protection.

angles.text: As a hunter, you leave behind the fight alone and stand beside a loyal companion. This rite completes your first training as a warden of the wilderness.
As shu'halo, you take an animal companion into battle with a sacred duty to care for it and respect the Earthmother's creations.
